mentions.text: during the whole of a dull dark and soundless day in the autumn of the year when the cloud hang oppressively low in the heaven i have be pass alone on horseback through a singularly dreary tract of country and at length find myself as the shade of the evening draw on within view of the melancholy house of usher i know not how it wasbut with the first glimpse of the building a sense of insufferable gloom pervade my spirit i say insufferable for the feeling be unrelieve by any of that half pleasurable because poetic sentiment with which the mind usually receive even the stern natural image of the desolate or terrible i look upon the scene before meupon the mere house and the simple landscape feature of the domain upon the bleak wallsupon the vacant eye like window upon a few rank sedgesand upon a few white trunk of decay treeswith an utter depression of soul which i can compare to no earthly sensation more properly than to the after dream of the reveller upon opiumthe bitter lapse into every day lifethe hideous dropping off of the veil there be an iciness a sinking a sickening of the heartan unredeemed dreariness of thought which no goading of the imagination could torture into aught of the sublime what be iti pause to thinkwhat be it that so unnerved i in the contemplation of the house of usher it be a mystery all insoluble nor could i grapple with the shadowy fancy that crowd upon i as i ponder i be force to fall back upon the unsatisfactory conclusion that while beyond doubt there be combination of very simple natural object which have the power of thus affect we still the analysis of this power lie among consideration beyond our depth it be possible i reflect that a mere different arrangement of the particular of the scene of the detail of the picture would be sufficient to modify or perhaps to annihilate its capacity for sorrowful impression and act upon this idea i rein my horse to the precipitous brink of a black and lurid tarn that lie in unruffled lustre by the dwelling and gaze downbut with a shudder even more thrilling than beforeupon the remodelled and invert image of the gray sedge and the ghastly tree stem and the vacant and eye like window nevertheless in this mansion of gloom i now propose to myself a sojourn of some week its proprietor roderick usher have be one of my boon companion in boyhood but many year have elapse since our last meeting a letter however have lately reach i in a distant part of the countrya letter from himwhich in its wildly importunate nature have admit of no other than a personal friend with a view of attempt by the cheerfulness of my society some alleviation of his malady it be the manner in which all this and much more be saidit be the apparent heart that go with
